newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS--Anaheim $513 mln revs priced.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS--Anaheim $513 mln revs priced.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds stagnated around unchanged in early afternoon trade on Tuesday as a lack of new California offerings was expected to firm demand for a $513 million Anaheim Public Finance Authority revenue bond sale.
The top tax-exempt yield in the offering was 5.83 percent in 2037, according to the lead underwriter, PaineWebber Inc.
"The levels to me look attractive, but it's a lot of size, they probably have built in some premium for the size," a trader said.
Traders said the large sale, which includes taxable bonds, likely would get the benefit from the rather unusual drought in new California municipal bonds that has been seen over the past few months.

"Historically, California has been one of the largest issuing states and consequently, one of the largest in demand. Supply has not been able to keep pace with demand because there have been so few deals," the trader said.

He added that competitively sold California offerings were fetching the same sorts of prices as the highest quality issues. While this week's supply calender includes additional offerings from California issuers, the volume of new paper from the state was expected to tail off after these issues come to the market.

Negotiated offerings for California counties slated for this week include Contra Costa County, Calif., which plans to sell $143 million of revenue bonds, while Riverside County was expected to sell $92 million of revenue bonds.
Competitive offerings for California include $130 million of Fresno Unified School District issues on February 6.
Elsewhere in the market on Tuesday, municipal traders largely dismissed the latest economic reports, which included new home sales and the leading indicators.
New home sales in December came in at an annualized rate of 783,000, above the 745,000 rate predicted by economists in a Reuters consensus survey.
And the leading indicators for December showed a 0.1 percent rise, matching predictions.
The market also looked ahead to the end on Wednesday of a two-day meeting by the Federal Reserve's policy-making arm, though the central bank was expected to leave interest rates unchanged.

March U.S. Treasury bond futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade eased two ticks to 112-1/32, while March municipal bond futures fell three ticks to 115-24/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 119 ticks.

In the secondary market, actively traded issues included Dade County, Florida, Water and Sewer System Revenues of October 2026, which were bid at 5.68 percent NET, unchanged. They pay a coupon of 5-1/4 percent.
And Intermountain Power Agency Utah Power Supply Revenues of July 2021, which pay a five percent coupon, were bid at 5.76 percent NET, flat.
